 LeBron's relationship with Luka Doncic questioned after good 76ers start 
 2026-11-04 08:31 
 After leaving the Lakers, LeBron James is thriving in a complementary role alongside Tyrese Maxey with the 76ers. Although his scoring average has dipped to 16.2 points, James is visibly happier embracing Maxey's lead for a genuine title chance, according to NBA analyst Bill Simmons.
 Credit: AP/Scanpix 
 Credit AP/Scanpix

 The Philadelphia 76ers and Los Angeles Lakers have started their seasons quite successfully after LeBron James left California for the East Coast.

 One of the arguments for this is how different the relationships between Luka Doncic , Tyrese Maxey and LeBron are.
 James has embraced whatever role the 76ers give him, as he can see that the team is capable to make a serious run to the NBA Finals, opposite to the Lakers last season, according to NBA analyst Bill Simmons .
 "LeBron seems like, you can see the light bulb going off with him, like 'holy sh*t, I might actually have a chance to make the finals and yeah, I'll play some center,'" Simmons said.
 "He seems super happy, he obviously has a great relationship with Maxey. I don't think the relationship with Luka was good. And I think we can safely say that.
 "LeBron last year seemed pretty miserable the whole season and knew it wasn't his team. This time he knew it was Maxey's team, he signed up for it."
 LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey Credit Getty Images via AFP - Scanpix LeBron James Sixers stint so far
 James has been playing a very similar amount of minutes per game with the Philadelphia 76ers as he did last season with the Lakers, however, his production has dropped.
 In the 2025-26 season, LeBron averaged 21.3 points, 6.2 rebounds and 7.2 assists in almost 34 minutes per game, while this season he is averaging 16.2 points, 7.0 rebounds and 7.3 assists in 33 minutes per game.
 The veteran superstar's scoring numbers have dropped as James has embraced a slightly smaller role with Philadelphia, acknowledging the 76ers as Maxey's team, as pointed out by Simmons.
